body: Egypt has very sparse coverage mostly in Generation 3; seven sections highlight historic places like pyramids, churches, and citadels with trekker cameras.
Many buildings in the trekker coverage area are made of sandstone, a common architectural material in Egypt.
The official language in Egypt is Arabic, recognizable by its script lines and dots seen on several signs in the trekker coverage.
The great pyramids of Giza are notable landmarks with trekker coverage, highlighting Egypt's rich historical heritage.
Inside the valley temple of Khafre, coverage is marked by rows of massive square pillars, a key architectural feature.
The Djoser pyramid, recognizable by stair-like sections and scaffolding, is located south of Cairo near minor historical excavation sites.
The Cairo Citadel is an enormous fortification with massive walls made of clean-cut sandstone blocks.
Inside the Citadel, you can see the Ottoman-era mosque with light grey domes and very tall minarets.
The trekker route around the normal urban Cairo street near the Hanging Church reveals a mix of historic sandstone walls and bustling city life.
Inside the Hanging Church is a beautiful courtyard adorned with religious mosaics and two white church spires.
The Qaitbay Citadel is a large castle surrounded by thick sandstone walls, a prominent coastal fortification.
The Saint Mina monastery complex features large palace-like buildings with numerous spires crowned with Christian crosses.
The Abu Mena Heritage Site is a major excavation area southwest of Alexandria, notable for a small yellow wooden chapel amidst historic ruins.
